chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنِ الْقَاسِمِ بْنِ الْبَطَلِ، الْحَارِثِيُّ، بَصْرِيّ.

translations.en: Abdullah ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Batal, al-Harithi, Basran.

chunks.arabic_text: كَذَّابٌ، غَالٍ، ضَعِيفٌ، مَتْرُوكُ الْحَدِيثِ، مَعْدُولٌ عَنْ ذِكْرِهِ.

translations.en: A liar, a ghālī (exaggerator), weak, (whose) hadith are abandoned, his mention is refrained from.

en.summary: This entry from Al-Ghadha'iri's *Kitab al-Du'afa* characterizes Abdullah ibn al-Qasim al-Harithi as a 'ghali' (exaggerator in religious matters), a trait often associated with early Shia sects like the Ghulat who attributed divine qualities to the Imams. His status as 'matruk' (abandoned) indicates that his narrations are generally rejected in favor of more reliable transmitters, reflecting the scholarly effort to preserve doctrinal purity by filtering out those prone to theological excess or fabrication.
en.seo_question: Who is Abdullah ibn al-Qasim ibn al-Batal and what is his status in hadith sciences?
